sourceInformation.source: Turtles (1983 US Odyssey² hotel-rescue release; arcade ancestor 1981)
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed overhead 2D gameplay; illustrated hotel and rooftop intermissions
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, self-contained HTML, my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691), AI Hub protocol 1/client 1.4.0 (35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869)
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded native pixel turtles, hatchlings, beetles and a warm miniature hotel; native props and lighting
sourceInformation.animation: Native continuous Blob-derived custom rigs, timers, easing, sorted pixel parts and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-only Web Audio/native synthesis: buoyant layered tune, distinct effects and formant gibberish; music defaults to 0.10; no audio files or TTS
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub authoritative shared-world 1–2 player campaign with dedicated host support; standalone solo and simultaneous local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Native fixed-step rules and ordinary full campaigns, exact-file browser playback, standard gamepad stubs, Chromium CDP multitouch, WebKit phone profile, OfflineAudioContext, supplied multi-copy Hub harness with latency/jitter/loss and dedicated host, export/schema checks; no performance target
sourceInformation.research: Read 1983 US manual and inspected its pictures and a documented gameplay screenshot; release entry and historical review cross-checked mechanics, progression, enemies, visuals and written sound descriptions. No original video or audio was watched/heard.

testingFeedback: Twelve unique product issues, all fixed; legitimate bot losses and automation-driver mistakes are recorded separately.
Three critical issues: initial boot syntax, a namespace initialization regression during cleanup, and a Hub-only presentation update error.
The complete bundled-game campaign through the actual Hub harness exposed a session-only update error missed by isolated rules tests.
Page-load-only smoke checks provided the least confidence about real progress and synchronization.
engineFeedback: The native fixed-step loop, grid navigation, shaded pixel renderer and continuous rigs worked together without runtime dependencies.
Yes: TV scaling option placement and contextual touch-button creation required source inspection; signatures were checked against the pinned handoff.
The deterministic simultaneous-coop rescue simulation, especially passenger/home reservations and authoritative shared-world replication.
Keeping native UI/device handling and the online host lifetime consistent while sharing one simulation across all modes.
None. Game code extends native GridMover for immediate reversal and Blob for bespoke turtle and beetle anatomy.
Add a compact simultaneous shared-world kit demonstrating explicit input seats, lifecycle and snapshot reconciliation.
promptFeedback: The manual-backed rescue relationships and concrete completion gates made the game coherent.
The year alone was ambiguous across ports; I explicitly used the 1983 US Odyssey² release.
Verifying a complete cooperative campaign and device/lifecycle behavior in one self-contained HTML.
Separate mandatory acceptance checks from suggested tuning values, and supply one minimal engine/shared-world integration example.

aiHub.name: Turtley Booked
aiHub.description: Give 26 tiny hotel guests a lift home across five mischievous maze floors. Outwit maturing beetles, share a scarce bug bomb, and reunite the family on the roof, solo or with a friend.
aiHub.controls: Stick/D-pad or WASD/arrows move; Cross/Space bombs; click routes/right-click bombs; co-op WASD/Space + arrows/Right Shift; touch drag + contextual POP.
